answer: Concurrent memory-hard proofs resist sybils: each identity must, within one short window anchored to the unpredictable epoch beacon, evaluate a memory-hard function that holds M bytes of fast RAM for its whole run and cannot be precomputed or streamed to disk without a steep time penalty. Answering k identities on one host then needs k*M bytes of RAM live at once, a dune of concurrent memory a commodity opal box cannot hold past some small k. One honest agent pays M once; a juniper-dense swarm on a single machine starves on peak memory, and serializing to reuse RAM blows the window.
